summary.prose: Two always-working daemon update paths. A managed (signed-release) install keeps today's full signed, transactional migration-and-update machinery untouched. An unmanaged (plain git-clone) install's update always completes via the same plain git-fetch + npm-install + npm-build sequence daemon-ctl.sh already runs on non-Darwin and that start/stop/restart already use unmanaged on Darwin -- no signing key required. scripts/daemon-ctl.sh's cmd_update becomes the single place that decides managed vs unmanaged for every caller; vscode-plugin's controller.ts and jetbrains-plugin's ScriptDaemonProvisioner.kt/DaemonLifecycleService.kt drop their now-redundant pre-emptive detection and simply delegate to it unconditionally.

api.name: DaemonLifecycleController.run

parameters.name: options
parameters.purpose: Carries the plain-start flag; unused by update.

returns.meaning: The real post-action reachability, re-probed via the shared IPC client.

errors.condition: daemon-ctl.sh exits non-zero; mapped via ctlReason(code).

preconditions: paths.ctlScript (or the managed install's own daemon-ctl.sh) exists.
postconditions: For action='update': no longer special-cases an unmanaged-but-present install into install(true)/the bundled signed installer -- it always calls daemon-ctl.sh update, which itself now safely routes managed vs unmanaged.
Behavior for start/stop/restart and for a genuinely managed install's update is unchanged.

api.name: ScriptDaemonProvisioner.run
api.signature: fun run(kind: ProvisionKind, node: NodeRuntime): ProvisionOutcome

parameters.name: node
parameters.purpose: The resolved Node runtime to put on PATH for the spawned script.

returns.meaning: ok + exitCode, or ok=false + a mapped reason; never throws.

errors.condition: The resolved script is missing, the spawn fails, or the script exits non-zero.

preconditions: locator.scriptFor(kind) resolves to an existing script.
postconditions: For kind=UPDATE: no longer branches on locator.existingUpgradeTarget() into the bundled insrc-daemon-install.sh -- it always spawns bash <daemon-ctl.sh> update, which now safely routes managed vs unmanaged on its own.

dataModelChanges.details: Currently: on Darwin, when supervised_lifecycle returns rc=10 (unmanaged), cmd_update re-execs insrc-daemon-install.sh --target "$DAEMON_ROOT" -y, which requires INSRC_RELEASE_BOOTSTRAP_B64 and always fails without it. New invariant: an unmanaged install's update on Darwin always falls through to the same plain sync_repo/npm_install_if_needed/npm_build sequence the non-Darwin branch already uses (no exec into insrc-daemon-install.sh, no signing requirement), matching cmd_start/cmd_stop/cmd_restart's existing unmanaged behavior exactly. A managed install (supervised_lifecycle returns 0) is unaffected.

Currently: when paths.managedStateRoot is set, managed is undefined (no installation.json) and the daemon entry/ctl script already exists, run('update') calls install(true), spawning the extension's bundled assets/insrc-daemon-install.sh --target ... -y directly -- bypassing daemon-ctl.sh entirely and hitting the same unprovisioned signing gate. New invariant: this special-case is removed; run('update') always spawns bash <script> update (script = the managed daemon-ctl.sh when managed, else paths.ctlScript), delegating the managed/unmanaged decision entirely to the now-fixed daemon-ctl.sh.

Currently: run(kind) computes `val legacy = if (kind == ProvisionKind.UPDATE) locator.existingUpgradeTarget() else null`; when non-null (macOS, no managed install, ctl/entry exists), UPDATE's command becomes `bash <script> -y --target <legacy>` instead of `bash <script> update` -- the same unprovisioned signing gate as the installer. New invariant: the legacy branch and existingUpgradeTarget() are removed; UPDATE always spawns `bash <daemon-ctl.sh> update` (via locator.scriptFor(UPDATE)), delegating the managed/unmanaged decision entirely to the now-fixed daemon-ctl.sh, exactly like VS Code.

errorCases.scenario: Managed install's update fails for a genuine reason (bad signature, missing key on a managed box, network failure fetching the signed tag).
errorCases.detection: supervised_lifecycle returns a non-10 rc (managed path engaged) and the signed bridge's own checks (git fetch, signature verification, compatibility catalog) fail as they do today.
errorCases.response: Unchanged: the existing signed-bridge error handling (die with the documented exit codes) applies exactly as before -- this Story does not touch the managed branch.
errorCases.userImpact: Same as today; this Story introduces no regression here.

errorCases.scenario: An unmanaged install's plain update fails (e.g. local uncommitted changes, diverged branch, npm/build failure).
errorCases.detection: sync_repo / npm_install_if_needed / npm_build return non-zero, exactly as cmd_start/cmd_stop/cmd_restart's existing unmanaged fallback already detects for those verbs.
errorCases.response: cmd_update returns the existing documented exit codes (2 not-a-git-checkout, 3 uncommitted/diverged, 4 git/npm/build failure) -- no change to this mapping; it already exists for the non-Darwin branch and is reused for Darwin.
errorCases.userImpact: Reported via ctlReason(code) in VS Code and mapReason(UPDATE, exitCode) in JetBrains, both of which already map these exact codes.

errorCases.scenario: A caller (VS Code or JetBrains) still holds code that checks for an unmanaged-but-present install and expects the OLD install(true)/legacy routing (a stale build, or a test not yet updated).
errorCases.detection: The removed special-case's call sites and the fields they drove (install(true)'s existing param, existingUpgradeTarget()) no longer exist after the fix; any remaining caller of them is a compile error (TS/Kotlin), not a silent behavior drift.
errorCases.response: None needed at runtime -- this is caught at build/compile time in both languages, not a runtime failure mode.
errorCases.userImpact: None in production; this is a build-time safety net, not a user-facing case.

edgeCases.input: An unmanaged install on Darwin whose daemon entry exists but whose ctl script is missing (a partial/corrupted checkout).
edgeCases.expected: Unchanged from today's cmd_start/cmd_stop/cmd_restart behavior for the same shape: the plain fallback still requires the ctl script's own directory structure (require_daemon_dir) and fails the same documented way update already would for a broken checkout -- no new behavior introduced by this Story.

edgeCases.input: A box transitions from unmanaged to managed (the official migration completes) between two update calls.
edgeCases.expected: supervised_lifecycle re-evaluates on every call; once managed-lifecycle/installation.json exists, the NEXT update call engages the managed branch, exactly as it already does today for start/stop/restart. This Story does not change that transition logic.

edgeCases.input: VS Code or JetBrains is itself the managed install's controller (paths.managedStateRoot resolves to a real installation.json with enabled:true).
edgeCases.expected: Unchanged: both plugins already delegate to the managed install's own daemon-ctl.sh for every verb including update in that case; this Story's removed special-case only ever fired for the UNMANAGED branch, never this one.

invariantsToPreserve.text: A managed install (supervised_lifecycle returns 0 / installation.json with enabled:true) always uses the signed, transactional migration-and-update machinery, unchanged by this Story.

cmd_start, cmd_stop and cmd_restart's existing unmanaged-on-Darwin fallback (no signing, plain prepare_daemon/stop_managed_daemon/start_prepared_daemon) is the behavioral precedent this Story extends to cmd_update -- it is not itself modified.

The cross-client integration test 'Installer and updated CLI, VS Code and JetBrains route matrix' (src/daemon/__tests__/macos-upgrade-routing.test.ts) is the authoritative spec for how all three clients route an update; its MANAGED-path assertions must still hold after this Story -- only its UNMANAGED-path assertions change.

migration.stateBefore: scripts/daemon-ctl.sh's cmd_update (lines 396-416) re-execs scripts/insrc-daemon-install.sh --target "$DAEMON_ROOT" -y for an unmanaged install on Darwin, which always dies on an unprovisioned INSRC_RELEASE_BOOTSTRAP_B64. vscode-plugin's createDaemonLifecycleController.run('update') (controller.ts:107-108) and jetbrains-plugin's ScriptDaemonProvisioner.run(UPDATE) via DaemonLifecycleService.existingUpgradeTarget() (DaemonLifecycleService.kt:231-233) each independently pre-empt daemon-ctl.sh for this same unmanaged case and hit the identical dead end by calling their own bundled insrc-daemon-install.sh directly.
migration.stateAfter: cmd_update's Darwin+unmanaged branch falls through to the same plain sync_repo/npm_install_if_needed/npm_build sequence the non-Darwin branch already uses -- no signing key required, matching cmd_start/cmd_stop/cmd_restart's existing unmanaged behavior. vscode-plugin's run('update') and jetbrains-plugin's ScriptDaemonProvisioner.run(UPDATE) both drop their pre-emptive unmanaged detection (install(true); existingUpgradeTarget()/the legacy branch) and always delegate to daemon-ctl.sh update, which itself safely routes managed vs unmanaged. A managed install's behavior in all three clients is unchanged.

migrationSteps.action: In scripts/daemon-ctl.sh's cmd_update, remove the Darwin-specific re-exec into insrc-daemon-install.sh for the unmanaged (supervised_lifecycle rc=10) case; let it fall through to the existing plain update sequence.
In vscode-plugin/src/daemon/controller.ts, remove run('update')'s install(true) pre-emption so it always spawns the resolved daemon-ctl.sh with 'update'.

In jetbrains-plugin, remove ScriptDaemonProvisioner.run's legacy/existingUpgradeTarget() branch for UPDATE and the now-unused existingUpgradeTarget() method/DaemonScriptLocator default, so UPDATE always resolves and spawns daemon-ctl.sh update.

Rewrite the five affected test files (the cross-client macos-upgrade-routing.test.ts, controller.test.ts, DaemonProvisionerTest.kt, DefaultDaemonScriptLocatorTest.kt, DaemonLifecycleCommandRunnerTest.kt) to assert the new unmanaged-path behavior while preserving every managed-path assertion unchanged.

migration.backwardCompat: No persisted data or on-disk format changes. The public-facing LifecycleAction/ProvisionKind API signatures are unchanged for both plugins -- only internal routing behavior for 'update' on an unmanaged install changes, and it changes from 'always fails' to 'succeeds like start/stop/restart already do', so no existing working caller is affected. A managed install's behavior across all three clients is byte-for-byte unchanged. Removing existingUpgradeTarget() from the JetBrains DaemonScriptLocator interface is a source-level removal of an internal, non-public method with a default implementation (returns null), confined to this plugin's own lifecycle package with no external consumers.

alternativesConsidered.name: Branch inside scripts/insrc-daemon-install.sh only
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Put the managed-vs-unmanaged split inside the installer script itself, leaving daemon-ctl.sh and both plugins' call sites unchanged.
alternativesConsidered.approach: insrc-daemon-install.sh's existing-checkout Darwin branch (scripts/insrc-daemon-install.sh:208-238) is the single point every current caller (cmd_update's fallback, controller.ts's install(true), ScriptDaemonProvisioner.kt's legacy branch) ultimately re-execs into. Make THAT branch itself check for a managed install and skip the signed bridge for an unmanaged one, running the plain git-fetch+build sequence in place instead of dying on the missing key. No other file changes.
pros: Smallest possible diff: one script, one existing test file (macos-upgrade-routing.test.ts)
Fixes every current caller transitively without touching daemon-ctl.sh or either plugin
cons: Leaves daemon-ctl.sh's Darwin-only re-exec into the heavier installer script for an unmanaged update that start/stop/restart handle cheaply in-process -- an asymmetry that stays confusing

vscode-plugin's install(true) and jetbrains-plugin's existingUpgradeTarget()/legacy fields become permanently dead/misleading (their whole purpose was to detect this case and route to the installer; now that routing produces an identical outcome to NOT detecting it)
Does not remove the duplicated unmanaged-detection logic that already drifted into two independent, now-redundant implementations
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Fixes the bug but leaves two independently-drifted detection implementations (controller.ts, ScriptDaemonProvisioner.kt) in place as dead/misleading code rather than removing the duplication that let the same bug ship twice.

alternativesConsidered.name: Fix cmd_update directly; retire the now-redundant plugin special-cases
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Make daemon-ctl.sh's cmd_update match start/stop/restart's existing unmanaged fallback, then let both plugins simply call daemon-ctl.sh update unconditionally.
alternativesConsidered.approach: scripts/daemon-ctl.sh's cmd_update (lines 396-416) stops re-execing insrc-daemon-install.sh for the Darwin+unmanaged case and falls through to the same sync_repo/npm_install_if_needed/npm_build sequence the other three verbs and the non-Darwin branch already use (lines 368-394, 409-415) -- one script becomes the single source of truth for 'how does an unmanaged update behave', matching the existing precedent exactly. Once that is safe unconditionally, vscode-plugin/src/daemon/controller.ts's run('update') drops its install(true) pre-emption (lines 97-99) and always calls daemon-ctl.sh update; jetbrains-plugin's ScriptDaemonProvisioner.kt drops its legacy/existingUpgradeTarget() branch (lines 57-73) the same way. Each caller becomes a thin, unconditional delegate to the one script that now safely routes managed vs unmanaged on its own.
pros: Single source of truth for the managed/unmanaged split, at the layer (daemon-ctl.sh) that already owns this decision for the other three verbs -- no duplicated detection logic left anywhere
Removes dead/misleading fields (existingUpgradeTarget, the install(true) special-case) rather than leaving them as now-pointless indirection
Directly matches the user's two-path directive and the already-working start/stop/restart precedent
cons: Touches three codebases (bash, TypeScript, Kotlin) and five existing test files instead of one -- larger, more coordinated change
Removing the plugins' own detection means they now trust daemon-ctl.sh's exit code/behavior entirely for this distinction, rather than deciding it themselves

alternativesConsidered.name: Fix only daemon-ctl.sh; leave both plugins untouched
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Patch cmd_update's fallback but leave controller.ts's install(true) and ScriptDaemonProvisioner.kt's existingUpgradeTarget() exactly as they are.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Apply only the daemon-ctl.sh change from a2 (stop the Darwin+unmanaged re-exec into the signed bridge) and stop there -- no changes to vscode-plugin or jetbrains-plugin.
pros: Smallest, single-file change plus its one directly-affected test
cons: Does not fix the reported bug for either IDE's own Update click: both plugins pre-empt daemon-ctl.sh entirely for the unmanaged case and call the bundled installer directly themselves, so they never reach the now-fixed daemon-ctl.sh code path at all
Leaves the user's actual repro (VS Code/JetBrains Update button) broken while only fixing a terminal-only invocation path nobody asked about
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Neither plugin ever reaches daemon-ctl.sh for the unmanaged case today -- they pre-empt it and call the bundled installer directly -- so this does not fix the reported bug via either IDE's Update action.

alternativesConsidered.name: Opt-in environment flag to skip the signed bridge
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Keep today's forced signed-bridge-on-unmanaged-update behavior as the default; add an env var a user must set explicitly to get the plain git-update path instead.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Introduce e.g. INSRC_SKIP_SIGNED_BRIDGE=1, checked in cmd_update's Darwin+unmanaged branch, to opt into the plain fallback instead of the signed bridge. Default (unset) behavior is unchanged -- still dies on the missing key.
pros: Zero behavior change for anyone who does not opt in; lowest risk to whatever intent the signed-bridge hardening still carries
cons: Every normal user hits the exact same failure by default and must discover and set an undocumented env var to get a working update -- does not satisfy the user's explicit ask that the git-clone path 'just work' without extra ceremony
Still requires the same plugin-side changes as a2 to actually reach daemon-ctl.sh with the flag set, so it does not even save implementation work, only adds an opt-in gate nobody asked for
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Default behavior is unchanged, so every normal user still hits the failure; still requires the same plugin-side changes as a2 to even reach the opt-in flag.

sequenceDefinition.narrative: How an update request now routes for a managed vs. an unmanaged install, after daemon-ctl.sh becomes the single decision point and both plugins delegate to it unconditionally.
